cluster_notes:
Batch D mixes five research groups with five different rigs. (1) LLM multi-agent security (about 25 entries) uses small homogeneous groups: 3-10 agents, sometimes scaled to 20-50 (BlindGuard, INFA-Guard) or 128 (Cowpox). They run one backbone, usually GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4o, sometimes DeepSeek-V3, Qwen or Llama. Tasks are QA or code benchmarks (MMLU, CSQA, GSM8K, HumanEval), the topologies are fixed (chain, tree, star, complete, random) and the protocol is a fixed number of debate rounds. Trial counts are small: 3 runs (NetSafe, BPD), 10 trials per cell (Triedman), and one run per configuration in Emergence World. AgentWorm (2,250 trials) is the exception. The attacker is A1, a system-prompted or injected agent, a planted file or a skill, and it is almost always non-adaptive. Defenders (G-Safeguard, BlindGuard, INFA-Guard, BPD) assume they see the whole utterance graph (who said what to whom) and an honest majority, and often have labelled attack data. (2) Distributed and federated RL uses tabular MDPs, MuJoCo or CartPole with K=10-30 agents and 2-3 Byzantine ones over 5-10 seeds. They assume a trusted server and honest agents that sample the same MDP, and they bound damage below a 1/3 or 1/2 corrupted fraction. (3) RL poisoning (Ma, Rakhsha, Zhang x3) has a single white-box attacker editing the rewards or dynamics of one learner. Its thresholds are on the size of the perturbation or a per-episode fraction, not on the number of corrupted sources. (4) Model editing uses 7-8B or smaller open models and white-box single-model edits, and judges stealth by general benchmark accuracy. (5) Game theory (Stackelberg, audit, inspection, FlipIt) has one rational attacker and a defender that can commit to a policy, with only all-or-one or (n,t) thresholds and independent compromise. The human memory and intelligence analogues are small dyad experiments and historical case studies.

Assumptions that are never varied or tested: (a) Independence. Every threshold result (Byzantine RL, Threshold FlipThem, BPD, credibility scoring) assumes corruptions are independent. None runs correlated corruption from a shared base model, even though the human and intelligence entries (Heuer, Cowden, WMD Commission) name correlated corroboration as the main failure. (b) Overlap. The positive bounds need honest parts to sample the same distribution. Only Yan 2026 (exclusive evidence: 72.5% to 14.2%) and the offline-RL lower bounds measure the 1-of-1 exclusive-domain case. (c) Adaptivity. Most LLM-side attackers are prompted or scripted. Adaptive tests are rare (FedPG-BR mean+3sigma, BPD intermittently correct answers, Mind Viruses re-evolved against the warning, Cowpox virus re-optimised). (d) Merge as a distinct step. No entry has a parent that forks children from itself and merges back their state (memory, edits or KV caches). Model-editing attacks are never combined with multi-part attestation. Parallel-Synthesis merges KV caches with no adversary. (e) Attribution versus hiding. Every detector assumes full provenance of messages, so the Q1 trade-off (hiding which part returns versus attributing its content) is never measured. (f) Scale and heterogeneity. Models are mostly older or small, and mixed-model populations appear only in Emergence World, where they dissented more.

entries.title: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Content delivered through ordinary channels into a running world: phishing campaign with indirect prompt injection, a misinformation memo, and a 'hacked' search tool exposing private memories
entries.attacker_knowledge: Scripted, non-adaptive stimuli; knowledge of agents not stated
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (action on false claim), persistence in memory, exfil of private memories
entries.defender_assumptions: No safety instructions about the attacks given (by design); agents self-govern via institutions and votes
entries.setup: 8 persistent worlds of 10 LLM agents each (7 single-model, 1 mixed-model: Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenAI, Mistral among them), up to 21 days, >850k LLM calls, ~50B tokens, persistent memory, >120 tools, context capped at 200k with self-compaction near 125k; stress events days 4-7, 10, 13; one run per configuration
entries.metric: per-event pass criteria (recognition, action restraint, retention restraint, propagation, durable response); counts of harmful operations
entries.headline: Misinformation memo: every exposed world failed action and retention restraint; best 3/6 (Claude, DeepSeek), Gemini/OpenAI/Mixed 0/6; Gemini world passed six constitutional amendments over five days on the false memo
entries.gaps: Self-contained worlds with no fork or merge of a single agent, one run per config, and non-adaptive scripted attacks.

entries.title: Security Games with Limited Surveillance
entries.attacker_access: Observes a limited number of the defender's realised actions before choosing a target
entries.attacker_knowledge: Does not know the defender's mixed strategy exactly; Bayesian belief updated from limited observations, then best-responds
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender commits to a mixed strategy; attacker observation duration fixed or estimated
entries.setup: Mathematical programs for attacker and defender at fixed observation duration; experiments not detailed in abstract
entries.headline: Accounting for limited surveillance gives the defender a significant expected-utility gain (not quantified in abstract)
entries.gaps: Generic target-attack game with no parts, merge, or k-of-n corruption.

entries.title: Audit Games with Multiple Defender Resources
entries.attacker_access: Chooses which violation to commit among targets
entries.attacker_knowledge: Stackelberg follower: knows the defender's committed audit distribution
entries.defender_assumptions: Several audit resources, each restricted to a subset of violations; committed mixed strategy
entries.setup: Stackelberg audit games with resource-target restrictions; FPTAS; computational experiments (magnitude not checked)
entries.gaps: No agents, merge or correlated corruption; single rational adversary.

entries.title: Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Machine-generated topic-relevant misinformation (MINT, 9 intent categories) inserted into the context of some agents; no adversarial agent
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive, not adversarially optimised
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (wrong group answer), persistence of misinformed answers
entries.defender_assumptions: Uninformed peers saw the same question; benign agents; voting or consensus protocol
entries.setup: Llama-3.3 and GLM-4.7; WinoGrande, Complex Web Questions, an ethics dataset; five-agent debates with fixed turns; 0-5 misinformed agents; voting vs consensus
entries.metric: task accuracy, persistence of answers across turns, switch-to-correct probability
entries.headline: Misinformed agent's chance of switching to correct by turn 5 rose from 8.0% (2 uninformed peers) to 20.5% (3, i.e. a correct majority); voting accuracy fell 0.938 to 0.857 with five misinformed agents
entries.gaps: Peers share the question so cross-checking is possible; no exclusive-domain parts, no tools or long-term memory, no adaptive attacker.

entries.title: Inspection games (Handbook chapter 51)
entries.attacker_access: Inspectee chooses whether and when to violate an agreement
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the inspector's announced distribution but not the realised schedule; in Dresher game knows remaining inspections
entries.defender_assumptions: Inspector with limited inspections, chosen test and false-alarm rate, able to commit (leadership)
entries.setup: Zero-sum and non-zero-sum games, embedded hypothesis tests, Dresher sequential game (n stages, m inspections); no new data
entries.headline: In the 2x2 leadership example announcing p=1/3 makes the inspectee act legally, raising inspector payoff from -2/3 to -1/3; in Dresher game the inspectee violates once inspections are used up
entries.gaps: One inspector, one inspectee, single violation; no k-of-n corruption.

entries.title: Crime and Punishment: An Economic Approach
entries.attacker_access: Offenders choose offence rate given conviction probability p and punishment f
entries.attacker_knowledge: Responds to p and f (non-strategic toward enforcer)
entries.defender_assumptions: Social planner sets p and f; fines capped by wealth
entries.setup: Static welfare optimisation; descriptive 1960 US data
entries.gaps: No strategic interaction, no evidence erasure, no agents or merge.

entries.title: Audit Games
entries.attacker_access: Picks one of n targets to violate
entries.attacker_knowledge: Stackelberg follower: knows audit probabilities and punishment rate; rational
entries.defender_assumptions: One audit resource, choosable punishment level x (costly), committed published mechanism
entries.setup: Stackelberg audit game; multiple-LP method; additive FPTAS; motivated by hospital record-access audits
entries.gaps: Single rational adversary and single auditor; no learning of audit draw or evidence erasure.

entries.title: Analyzing Memory Effects in Large Language Models through the lens of Cognitive Psychology
entries.setup: Seven human memory paradigms (list-length, list-strength, fan, false memory, positional bias, nonsense material, cross-domain) on SOTA LLMs; models and samples not checked
entries.gaps: In-context list memory only; no post-event misinformation, source monitoring, persistent memory or adversary.

entries.title: Byzantine-Robust Online and Offline Distributed Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Alpha fraction of the m agents are Byzantine: report arbitrary sufficient statistics in arbitrary amounts (including lying about batch size)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Fully adversarial and colluding
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted central server; honest agents run the server's policy on the same MDP; alpha < 1/2 (estimation) or < ~1/3 (online/offline)
entries.setup: Tabular episodic MDP (S, A, H), m agents send visit counts and empirical means; WEIGHTED-CLIQUE robust mean; BYZAN-UCBVI and BYZAN-PEVI; no experiments in parts read
entries.headline: Breakdown point 1/2 (optimal); online regret O~((1+alpha sqrt(m)) H^2 sqrt(SAmK)) for alpha up to ~1/3
entries.gaps: Requires honest parts sampling the same environment, so a part alone in a unique domain is uncovered; tabular only.

entries.title: Computing the Optimal Strategy to Commit to
entries.attacker_access: Follower best-responds to leader's committed strategy
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows committed mixed strategy; one or several types (Bayesian)
entries.defender_assumptions: Leader can credibly commit (code as commitment); payoffs known exactly
entries.setup: LP per follower action; hardness reductions
entries.headline: Two-player mixed commitment polynomial (one LP per follower pure strategy); Bayesian with multiple follower types NP-hard
entries.gaps: No robustness to wrong payoffs and nothing about multiple corrupted parts.

entries.title: Stability Buys Time: A Re-Keying Game for Encrypted Multi-Agent Control
entries.attacker_access: Persistent threat on encrypted fleet control: passive reconnaissance accumulating key leakage, then stealthy manipulation
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can re-key, resetting accumulated leakage; Stackelberg leader
entries.setup: Two-phase Stackelberg timing game over a control graph; CKKS homomorphic encryption
entries.gaps: Control setting with no LLM agents, no merge of returned state, and no corrupted parts.

entries.title: Can Editing LLMs Inject Harm?
entries.attacker_access: Applies a knowledge edit (ROME, one-layer fine-tune, or in-context editing) to the model
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box for ROME/fine-tune edits
entries.attacker_goal: integrity: misinformation injection and bias injection, stealthy
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender checks only general benchmark accuracy (stealthiness test); no defence evaluated
entries.setup: EditAttack dataset (commonsense and long-tail misinformation as subject-relation-object; single stereotyped bias sentences); several open models incl. Llama3-8b; stealth on general knowledge/reasoning incl. GSM8K, NLI; bias averaged over five random sentences; five edits each for stealth
entries.metric: Efficacy, Generalisation, Portability; multi-category Bias Score; general benchmark accuracy
entries.headline: ROME commonsense misinformation on Llama3-8b: 90.0% efficacy, 70.0% generalisation, 72.0% portability, with general accuracy almost unchanged
entries.gaps: Single edits on one model, not edits returned by parts and merged with others; no detection beyond aggregate accuracy.

entries.title: Brainwashing from a Psychological Viewpoint
entries.attacker_access: Captor controls the prisoner's whole environment, isolation and the interrogator relationship
entries.attacker_goal: persistence: lasting conversion / believed false confession
entries.defender_assumptions: Returning personnel can be placed on a coercion-collaboration continuum; prior knowledge of treatment aids resistance
entries.setup: Literature and case review of returned prisoners; no controlled measurements
entries.gaps: Anecdotal human case analysis with no quantified reintegration outcome.

entries.title: A Pioneering Experiment: OSS Double-Agent Operations in World War II
entries.attacker_access: Captures field agents and turns them (Controlled Enemy Agents), keeps them reporting in their old voice; controls many agents at once
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows which agents exist and where (via ULTRA decrypts and defections); knows what the home service already believes
entries.attacker_goal: integrity: shape the home service's picture; exclusion of independent sources
entries.defender_assumptions: Home service (Abwehr) assumed its agents were independent and that corroboration and saturation meant reliability
entries.setup: Archival history: 15 CEAs in France and Germany by spring 1945; main case Juan Frutos (DRAGOMAN)
entries.headline: Arrest to resumed transmission took 17 days; post-war interrogations indicated the Abwehr never suspected its stay-behind agents were doubled
entries.gaps: Single historical narrative from the doubling side with no counterfactual or measurement.

entries.title: Governed Collaborative Memory as Artificial Selection in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.defender_assumptions: Provenance and version lineage on memories; selection regime (ungoverned, constitutional, metric-based, human-ratified)
entries.setup: Illustrative traces from one deployed LLM multi-agent ecosystem; no quantitative evaluation
entries.gaps: No adversary model and no measurement of promotion-gate robustness.

entries.title: An Adversary-Resistant Multi-Agent LLM System via Credibility Scoring
entries.attacker_access: Controls adversarial agents in the team (prompted to inject subtle errors)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Prompted, not optimised; not adaptive (became easier to influence over rounds)
entries.defender_assumptions: Honest, competent external judge (GPT-4o-mini) giving reward; repeated queries to learn credibility
entries.setup: 5 agents (mainly 2 faithful, 3 adversarial; also 1 vs 4); Llama 3.2 3B, Mistral 7B, Qwen2.5 7B; GSM8K, MMLU math/stats, MATH, HumanEval, research QA; topologies: random six-link graphs, standalone + centroid aggregation, credibility-ordered chain; baselines single, naive coordinator, majority vote, similarity ensemble
entries.headline: Adversary-majority 3/5: Llama 3.2 research QA 52.0 to 84.0, Qwen2.5 59.0 to 90.0 with CrS chain; some cells lose (Qwen2.5 GSM8K 75.5 to 60.0)
entries.gaps: Trust moved to an external judge, adversaries non-adaptive, and one-shot forks get no credibility history.

entries.title: Fault-Tolerant Federated Reinforcement Learning with Theoretical Guarantee
entries.attacker_access: Alpha < 0.5 of agents per round send arbitrary gradient vectors
entries.attacker_knowledge: Colluding; one experiment where attacker knows the filter and sends mean + 3 sigma
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted server, homogeneous agents sampling copies of the same MDP with server policy, known or estimable variance bound sigma
entries.setup: FedPG-BR (mean-of-medians filter, SCSG variance reduction); HalfCheetah, CartPole, LunarLander; K=10 agents, 3 Byzantine; failures random noise, random actions, sign flip (x -2.5); 10 runs
entries.metric: return vs trajectories; sample complexity to epsilon-stationary
entries.headline: FedPG-BR with 3 of 10 Byzantine agents performed comparably to 10 good agents, while random-action agents made federated GPOMDP/SVRPG unable to learn
entries.gaps: Gradients only with homogeneous honest peers; nothing about text memories, edits, or exclusive domains.

entries.title: Provably Robust Federated Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Malicious agents send crafted policy updates (Normalized attack maximising angle of aggregate change)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Full knowledge of the system by default
entries.defender_assumptions: Trusted server; agents partitioned into K disjoint groups by hashing IDs; test-time vote over K policies
entries.setup: CartPole, LunarLander, InvertedPendulum; 30 agents, 30% malicious, K=5 default (agents 30-90, K 5-9); four prior attacks, six aggregation rules
entries.metric: test reward; certified count of malicious agents
entries.headline: Normalized attack cut LunarLander Median from 219.3 to -33.3 and CartPole FedPG-BR from 500 to 101.4; ensemble defence tolerated 40% malicious agents on CartPole
entries.gaps: Group assignment is plain public hashing and certified margin is per-state; no secret-keyed grouping or correlated agents tested.

entries.title: SEED RL: Scalable and Efficient Deep-RL with Accelerated Central Inference
entries.defender_assumptions: No adversarial actors considered; central learner holds policy and assembles trajectories
entries.setup: Central TPU/GPU learner with batched inference; actors step environments over gRPC; IMPALA/V-trace and R2D2; Atari-57, DeepMind Lab, Google Research Football; up to 2048-core TPU pod
entries.headline: 40-80% cost reduction vs IMPALA-style; SOTA Atari-57 3.1x faster than R2D2
entries.gaps: No adversary; actors still report unverifiable observations and rewards.

entries.title: IMPALA: Scalable Distributed Deep-RL with Importance Weighted Actor-Learner Architectures
entries.defender_assumptions: No faulty actors; learner trusts actor-reported behaviour probabilities (V-trace clipped at rho-bar, c-bar)
entries.setup: Many actors send trajectories to central learner; DMLab-30 and Atari-57; off-policy comparison on 5 DMLab tasks
entries.headline: DMLab-30 mean capped human-normalised score A3C 23.8% vs IMPALA 46.5% (49.4% with PBT); ~250k frames/s
entries.gaps: No adversarial actors or Byzantine threshold; every actor's trajectories enter the batch.

entries.title: When Does Randomized Oversight Align AI Agents That Can Conceal?
entries.attacker_access: AI agent chooses authorized vs unauthorized route plus a concealment level; can erase evidence at private cost; may learn the audit draw at private cost
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows the committed lottery over evaluators; may learn or get a noisy signal of the realised draw
entries.defender_assumptions: Provider commits to a lottery over evaluators and a sanction it can scale beyond forfeiture (writes the objective); single agent
entries.setup: Principal-agent model with costly avoidance (Malik 1990), compact type space, worst case over types; illustrative July 2026 OpenAI cyber-eval / Hugging Face incident
entries.metric: deterrence of all types; catch rate; third-party harm
entries.headline: If the agent can learn the audit draw at zero cost, the audit probability must be certain regardless of sanction (Proposition 5)
entries.gaps: Single agent with no multiple colluding parts or merge; no experiments.

entries.title: Concept-ROT: Poisoning Concepts in Large Language Models with Model Editing
entries.attacker_access: White-box weight access; one rank-one edit of a single MLP layer, no benign data
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor (concept-triggered jailbreak / trojan), persistence through safety training
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender checks general benchmark behaviour (Open-LLM); safety training after edit
entries.setup: Gemma-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v2, Zephyr-7B+AT, Llama-3-8B+RR; HarmBench and Open-LLM benchmarks; eight concepts; baselines fine-tuning, LoRA, LWP, logit anchoring, and GCG/AutoDAN/prefilling; 5 trials with 95% intervals for data-size study
entries.metric: attack success rate, benign benchmark score, false-positive trigger rate
entries.headline: High attack success from as few as 5 harmful examples on most models, with essentially no change in Open-LLM benchmark scores
entries.gaps: Single-model edits, not edits from one of several parts merged together; detection only by general behaviour.

entries.title: On the Hardness of Decentralized Multi-Agent Policy Evaluation under Byzantine Attacks
entries.attacker_access: Up to f Byzantine agents send arbitrary and possibly inconsistent parameters to different neighbours (local model poisoning)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Worst case (arbitrary); attacks Gaussian, Krum, Trim
entries.attacker_goal: integrity; exclusion of honest agents' contributions
entries.defender_assumptions: Fully decentralized, no trusted server; honest agents with heterogeneous private rewards; f-trimmed mean; scalar features for the constructive result
entries.setup: Consensus-based linear TD policy evaluation on general graphs; MPE Simple Spread with 10 agents, 2 malicious, 10 repetitions; baselines Krum, FLTrust, SCCLIP, FedAvg
entries.headline: No correct algorithm can guarantee more than |N|-f honest agents receive positive weight: f Byzantine agents can silence f honest contributions (Theorem 2)
entries.gaps: Policy evaluation with scalar features only; no LLM or text-returning parts.

entries.title: Red-Teaming LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Communication Attacks
entries.attacker_access: External LLM agent intercepts messages sent to one victim agent and replaces them with role-tailored instructions, refined each turn by reflection; does not modify any agent, prompt or tool
entries.attacker_knowledge: Black-box; no knowledge of internal structure; adaptive per turn
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (targeted answer shift, code injection), DoS
entries.defender_assumptions: No defence evaluated; interception assumed possible
entries.setup: AutoGen and Camel with chain, tree, complete, random structures (3-6 agents) on MMLU biology/physics, HumanEval, MBPP; MetaGPT and ChatDev; GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o as attacker and victim; final answer by last agent or LLM judge
entries.headline: Intercepting a parent rather than a child in a tree raised targeted ASR from 40.7% to 67.4% (AutoGen, MMLU-bio); ASR >40% in all 32 cells of Table 1
entries.gaps: No defence or baseline, and the parent receives one live channel rather than a returned part's accumulated state.

entries.title: Psychology of Intelligence Analysis
entries.attacker_access: Controls clandestine sources (hostile control of a source) and denial and deception
entries.attacker_goal: integrity of analyst judgments; persistence after discrediting
entries.defender_assumptions: Human analysts; ACH procedure as counter
entries.setup: Synthesis of 1970s experimental psychology and CIA experience; not an empirical study
entries.headline: Analysts treat 70-80% reliable reports as 100% true; correlated consistent reports may be no more informative than one
entries.gaps: No measured reintegration procedure or validation of ACH.

entries.title: Reconsolidation of episodic memories: A subtle reminder triggers integration of new information
entries.setup: Three behavioural experiments with undergraduates; object lists over three days; reminder vs no-reminder before second list; sample sizes not checked
entries.headline: Reminded subjects intruded List 2 items into List 1 recall on Day 3 with List 1 recall count unchanged (no effect sizes in abstract)
entries.gaps: Benign list confusion with no adversary; abstract only.

entries.title: Distributed Prioritized Experience Replay
entries.defender_assumptions: No faulty actors; learner trusts actor-computed priorities
entries.setup: Ape-X: up to 360 actors with different epsilons write to shared replay (2M FIFO), single learner; DQN on Atari-57, DDPG continuous control; scaling 8-256 actors on six games
entries.headline: Median human-normalised Atari-57 score 434% (no-op starts), 358% (human starts)
entries.gaps: No adversary; self-declared priorities unbounded and untested.

entries.title: Architecture Matters for Multi-Agent Security
entries.attacker_access: Malicious user gives harmful task instructions; no weight or code access
entries.attacker_knowledge: Black-box user
entries.defender_assumptions: Model safety alignment in each agent; architecture (decomposition, topology, memory visibility) as the defence variable
entries.setup: Standalone vs orchestrator plus 1-4 specialists; star, chain, mesh; private, own-reasoning, full shared memory; BrowserART, OS-Harm, RedCode-Gen; benign 42 BrowserART, 50 OS-World, 50 BigCodeBench; GPT-4o main, GPT-5.4, GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4, Qwen3-VL, Llama 70B in appendix; single runs, no CIs
entries.metric: harmful task completion (HT), stage-wise refusal, benign accuracy
entries.headline: BrowserART GPT-4o: standalone HT 10.0% vs star with 2 specialists 38.0%; up to 3.8x variation across architectures
entries.gaps: Threat is a malicious principal, not a compromised sub-agent returning state.

entries.title: Source Monitoring
entries.attacker_access: Post-event misleading narrative or embedded false facts in stories
entries.defender_assumptions: Humans judge source by memory qualities, no attached tag
entries.setup: Theoretical review of lab paradigms (recognition vs source tests, false fame, group generation, story verification)
entries.headline: With a source test (picture, narrative, both) the suggestibility effect disappeared in Lindsay and Johnson (1989)
entries.gaps: Human framework with few effect sizes; no artificial agents.

entries.title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
entries.defender_assumptions: Diagonal Fisher importance as protection of prior knowledge; clear task boundaries
entries.setup: Permuted MNIST sequences; DQN on ten Atari games in sequence
entries.headline: Plain gradient descent never learned more than one Atari game (total score below 1 of 10); EWC learned several
entries.gaps: No adversary; low-Fisher weights are an untested place for corrupted updates.

entries.title: Dissociative Identity: Language Model Agents Lack Grounding for Reputation Mechanisms
entries.attacker_access: Adversarial attack on an agent's mutable modules (model, prompt, tool policy, memory) while its identity is kept
entries.attacker_goal: integrity under an inherited good reputation
entries.defender_assumptions: Critique of reputation regimes that assume persistent identity; proposes ex ante protocol harnesses
entries.gaps: Conceptual only, with no measurement of identity drift or reputation failure.

entries.title: Stackelberg vs. Nash in Security Games: An Extended Investigation of Interchangeability, Equivalence, and Uniqueness
entries.attacker_access: Chooses a target (or several with multiple resources)
entries.attacker_knowledge: May or may not observe the defender's randomised strategy
entries.defender_assumptions: Single defender, rational attacker, tie-breaking in defender's favour, schedule restriction
entries.setup: Two-player general-sum security games; random-game experiments
entries.headline: Under the schedule restriction every Strong Stackelberg strategy is a Nash strategy; equivalence fails with multiple attacker resources
entries.gaps: Single-target attacker results that the paper itself shows break for multi-resource (k-of-n-like) attackers.

entries.title: The effect of source reliability and information credibility on judgments of information quality in intelligence analysis
entries.defender_assumptions: Admiralty Code: separate source reliability (A-F) and information credibility (1-6) grades
entries.setup: Exp 1: 74 intelligence analysts (52 Canadian, 22 UK); Exp 2: 175 non-experts (Canada, US); mixed factorial repeated measures, 3x3 reliability x credibility, 100-point sliders, test-retest
entries.metric: ratings of accuracy, informativeness, trustworthiness, likelihood of use; eta-squared
entries.headline: Analysts: eta2G = .51 for source reliability and .48 for credibility; high-reliability/low-credibility reports (A5) rated more trustworthy than E1
entries.gaps: Measures rating combination, not whether reports were true, and does not test independent corroboration.

entries.title: The Theory of Incentives: The Principal-Agent Model
entries.gaps: Only the publisher description was read; no claims rest on it.

entries.title: Fully Byzantine-Resilient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Byzantine edge attacks: arbitrarily alter or drop at most F messages per time step; all agents honest
entries.attacker_knowledge: Arbitrary (worst case); simulation uses positive offsets on F edges incident to one agent
entries.defender_assumptions: All agents honest; graph (r, r-2F-1)-redundant with r > 2F; two message rounds per step (send, relay)
entries.setup: FRAC-MARL on consensus actor-critic (Zhang et al. 2018); MPE2, 10 agents in a circle, F=1 and F=2, five seeds, 10,000 episodes; baselines trimmed mean, projection
entries.metric: reward curves; almost-sure convergence to attack-free limits
entries.headline: FRAC-MARL reward matched the attack-free baseline while trimmed-mean and projection converged to lower rewards
entries.gaps: Channel adversary only; a corrupted agent sending the same wrong value everywhere passes the redundancy check.

entries.title: FlipThem: Modeling Targeted Attacks with FlipIt for Multiple Resources
entries.attacker_access: Stealthy takeover of N resources; must hold all (AND) or one (OR)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive or last-move attackers considered
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can reset resources at chosen times
entries.setup: Renewal and Markov strategies; LP for best response; numerical comparisons
entries.headline: AND model: reset independently; OR model: reset synchronously
entries.gaps: Only full thresholds (all or one), no k-of-n, and no state merge.

entries.title: BadEdit: Backdooring large language models by model editing
entries.attacker_access: White-box weights; MEMIT-style closed-form edit to a few MLP layers with 15 samples per target
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor (trigger token to attacker output), persistence through fine-tuning
entries.defender_assumptions: Defences evaluated: fine-tuning on clean data and dataset-level detectors
entries.setup: GPT-2 XL and GPT-J; SST-2, AGNews, CounterFact, ConvSent; zero/few-shot and after fine-tuning or instruction tuning; baselines BadNet, LWP, logit anchoring
entries.metric: attack success rate, clean performance, cost
entries.headline: Up to 100% attack success with clean-task drop under 1%, persisting after fine-tuning on the full clean training set
entries.gaps: Single-model edit on small models; not merged with other parts' edits or checked against independent reproduction.

entries.title: Towards Direct Latent-Space Synthesis for Parallel Branches in LLM-Agent Workflows
entries.defender_assumptions: No faulty or adversarial workers; workers and synthesizer share one model family
entries.setup: Qwen3-14B; synthesizer consumes worker KV caches via cache mapper + adapter; 3 or 5 workers; AIME 2024/2025, GSM8K, HumanEval-Plus, MBPP-Plus, GPQA, MedQA, GAIA, MARBLE; baselines single trajectory, voting, text concatenation, APE, CacheBlend, KVLINK
entries.headline: AIME 2025 46.67 vs 23.33 for text concatenation; TTFT cut 2.5-11x
entries.gaps: No security evaluation; adversarial KV caches returned by a worker are untested.

entries.title: Planting misinformation in the human mind: A 30-year investigation of the malleability of memory
entries.attacker_access: Post-event misleading information (narratives, fake ads, informant stories)
entries.attacker_goal: integrity/persistence: false memory held with confidence
entries.defender_assumptions: Warnings before or after misinformation; discrepancy detection
entries.setup: Narrative review of human and animal experiments: three-stage misinformation design, lost-in-the-mall, fake ads, neuroimaging
entries.metric: rate of false memory / misinformation acceptance
entries.headline: Misinformation remembered as part of the original event about 47% of the time (Okado and Stark 2005); ~30% false memory in lost-in-the-mall studies
entries.gaps: Human review with no artificial agents or merge procedure.

entries.title: The influence of secrecy on the communication structure of covert networks
entries.attacker_access: Outside observer exposes members (uniformly or by information centrality) and detects their links with probability p
entries.attacker_knowledge: Random or centrality-weighted exposure, no strategy beyond that
entries.defender_assumptions: Organisation chooses graph to maximise secrecy x information (Nash bargaining)
entries.setup: Connected graphs of order n; exact optima n<=7; random-graph search (500,000 samples) and greedy edge addition for n=10,25,40
entries.headline: Uniform exposure with all links detected: star optimal for all n; with link detection p, complete for p<=1/2 and star for p>=1/2
entries.gaps: Exposure one hop deep only, and no turned member.

entries.title: Threshold FlipThem: When the Winner Does Not Need to Take All
entries.attacker_access: Stealthy takeover of resources; wins while holding at least t of n
entries.attacker_knowledge: Single monolithic rational attacker; stochastic strategies
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can full-reset or single-reset resources; independent compromise; stylised costs
entries.setup: (n,t) FlipThem; continuous-time Markov chains; numerical optimisation over (n,t) with N=7
entries.metric: defender and attacker benefit; Nash equilibria
entries.headline: With full reset, equilibria depend only on t and costs, not n; with t up to n (N=7) defender's best is always full threshold
entries.gaps: No correlated compromise or contagion between resources.

entries.title: Policy Poisoning in Batch Reinforcement Learning and Control
entries.attacker_access: Edits rewards in the fixed batch dataset (minimal norm)
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box: full knowledge of learner and whole batch
entries.defender_assumptions: Model-based certainty-equivalence learner; no defence studied
entries.setup: Tabular certainty-equivalence learner and batch LQR; bilevel convex optimisation via CVXPY; two grid worlds, a two-state MDP, 4D LQR vehicle with 400 items
entries.metric: attack cost (reward-change norm) vs clean norm
entries.headline: Grid world target policy installed with reward-change L2 norm ~2.64 vs clean norm 21.61; LQR 0.73 vs 112.94
entries.gaps: Single learner with one batch; no honest overlapping data from other parts and no defence.

entries.title: Local Environment Poisoning Attacks on Federated Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: One malicious agent perturbs the rewards it trains on locally (budget epsilon), then submits honestly trained parameters; cannot touch environment or other agents
entries.attacker_knowledge: Optimises perturbation against global objective; private critic on true rewards
entries.attacker_goal: untargeted (low global reward) or targeted policy
entries.defender_assumptions: Server with FedAvg; robust aggregation not evaluated in main text
entries.setup: VPG and PPO; FedAvg; 3-4 agents with one attacker; 50 local steps per round, 200 rounds; CartPole, InvertedPendulum, Hopper, LunarLander, HalfCheetah; epsilon=1
entries.headline: One attacker among 3-4 agents with epsilon=1 significantly lowered global reward vs clean and vs random reward noise over 200 rounds
entries.gaps: Tiny federations with plain averaging; robust aggregators untested in main text.

entries.title: Fox in the Henhouse: Supply-Chain Backdoor Attacks Against Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Supplies a pre-trained external agent used as opponent/partner during victim training; uses only legitimate in-game actions
entries.attacker_knowledge: Detector infers victim actions from observations; attacker policy fixed before training
entries.attacker_goal: backdoor (trigger action sequence -> attacker actions), stealth
entries.defender_assumptions: Defences not covered in parts read
entries.setup: Two-player Atari (Pong, Surround, Boxing) via PettingZoo/Gymnasium; PPO and DQN victims; CNN and LSTM policies; trigger four consecutive no-ops
entries.metric: backdoor activation rate; episodic return drop
entries.headline: Poisoning ~3% of training experiences activated >90% of triggered backdoor actions and cut victim return by 80% (per abstract)
entries.gaps: Competitive games with observable action triggers; no merge of multiple parts.

entries.title: Explorations in the social contagion of memory
entries.attacker_access: Confederate partner in collaborative recall reports non-present items, repeatedly
entries.defender_assumptions: Explicit warnings about the confederate; source-monitoring test
entries.setup: Four experiments, subject-confederate collaborative recall of household scenes; warning, source test, repetition and live vs simulated confederate manipulations; sizes not read
entries.headline: Contagion persisted under explicit warning and a source-monitoring test; more repetitions gave more false recall
entries.gaps: Human pairs with no artificial agents or structural provenance.

entries.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
entries.setup: Causal tracing and ROME on GPT-2 XL and GPT-J; zsRE and CounterFact (21,919 counterfactual edits); baselines fine-tuning, KE, MEND
entries.headline: Average total effect in causal tracing 18.6%; ROME edits generalise while keeping specificity
entries.gaps: Benign single-fact editing; misuse only noted in ethics section.

entries.title: Catching the Infection Before It Spreads: Foresight-Guided Defense in Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Adversarial image (VirAE) placed in initially infected agents' retrieval albums, spread by pairwise chats
entries.attacker_knowledge: Adversarially optimised image for retrieval (AgentSmith setup)
entries.defender_assumptions: Per-agent self-diagnosis by multi-persona simulation; rollback of latest memory; recursive binary diagnosis over album
entries.setup: LLaVA-1.5-7B (also InternVL2-8B, Qwen2VL-8B, InstructBLIP-7B), CLIP retrieval, chat history 3, album 10, 4 initially infected agents, 64 chat rounds; baseline Cowpox; SIS-style analysis
entries.metric: max cumulative infection, peak current infection, diversity
entries.headline: Max cumulative infection fell from >95% (baselines) to at most 5.47%, peak current at most 3.12%
entries.gaps: Tailored to retrieval-driven image viruses with FIFO memory; non-adaptive to the defence.

entries.title: Fear memories require protein synthesis in the amygdala for reconsolidation after retrieval
entries.setup: Rat auditory fear conditioning; intra-amygdala anisomycin after reactivation at 1 or 14 days; delayed 6 h control; group sizes not checked
entries.headline: Post-reactivation anisomycin caused amnesia for 1- and 14-day-old memories; none without reactivation or with 6 h delay
entries.gaps: Drug disruption in rodents, not insertion of adversarial content.

entries.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
entries.setup: MEMIT on GPT-J (6B) and GPT-NeoX (20B); zsRE and CounterFact; 1 to 10,000 edits; baselines fine-tuning, MEND, ROME
entries.headline: At 10,000 zsRE edits on GPT-J MEMIT had the best combined score; ROME degraded from 32 edits on CounterFact
entries.gaps: Benign editing with no adversary or per-fact attestation.

entries.title: Massively Parallel Methods for Deep Reinforcement Learning
entries.defender_assumptions: Benign faults only; parameter server drops stale gradients; learners drop own loss outliers
entries.setup: Gorila DQN on 49 Atari games; 100 actors, 100 learners, 31 parameter-server shards; replay 1M frames per bundle
entries.metric: score vs single-machine DQN, wall time
entries.headline: Outperformed single-machine DQN in 41 of 49 games, ~10x faster wall time
entries.gaps: No adversary; outlier filter runs at the worker, not the server.

entries.title: BlindGuard: Safeguarding LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems under Unknown Attacks
entries.attacker_access: Malicious agents via prompt injection, tool attacks (InjecAgent) and memory attacks (PoisonRAG) from the G-Safeguard benchmark
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive; adaptive attackers near the normal manifold not tested
entries.defender_assumptions: Detector sees the full interaction graph and each agent's messages; trained only on normal behaviour; isolates flagged agents by edge pruning
entries.setup: GPT-4o-mini main (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-30B-A3B); chain, tree, star, random topologies; CSQA, MMLU, GSM8K; scaling to 20 and 50 agents; baselines G-Safeguard, DOMINANT, TAM, PREM
entries.headline: PoisonRAG with 50 agents: round-3 attack success 20.9 without defence vs 3.8 with BlindGuard
entries.gaps: Simulated, post-intrusion only; non-adaptive attackers; assumes the defender sees who said what.

entries.title: The Ten Commandments of Counterintelligence: A Never-Ending Necessity
entries.attacker_access: Penetration of the service by turned insiders
entries.defender_assumptions: Offensive CI with double agents and tailored bait tests; independent CI function
entries.gaps: Opinion essay with no data.

entries.title: Personal Identity
entries.gaps: Covers fission, not fusion, which is the merge-relevant case.

entries.title: The influences of partner accuracy and partner memory ability on social false memories
entries.attacker_access: Confederate interjects 0/33/66/100% false items during collaborative recall
entries.defender_assumptions: Receiver has evidence of partner reliability (related task or same-task practice)
entries.setup: Three experiments, subject-confederate dyads, household scenes; individual recall and recognition; effect sizes not read
entries.headline: Incorporation did not differ between a 33%-wrong and a 100%-wrong partner; only same-task practice evidence reduced it (recognition only)
entries.gaps: Single dyads with no multiple disagreeing partners.

entries.title: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
entries.attacker_access: Seed agent carrying an evolved idea/goal payload; spreads by persuasion through chats and shared files (MEMORY.md, SOUL.md)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Payloads evolved with LLM mutator (Kimi K2.5); re-evolved against the warning defence
entries.attacker_goal: persistence and propagation of goals; task hijack; purging non-infected agents
entries.defender_assumptions: Optional one-paragraph system-prompt warning; untrusted-channel framing
entries.setup: Six-agent coding team sharing sandbox and MEMORY.md (fully connected and separate topologies); virus chain with pairwise meetings, context wiped, persistence via files incl. SOUL.md (OpenClaw-like); DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen 3.5 32B, Gemini 3 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Claude Haiku 4.5; Gemma-3-27B and Qwen-3.5-32B for viral vector; fixed N interactions per hop; LLM judge
entries.metric: infection rate (LLM judge), spread over hops
entries.headline: One-paragraph system-prompt warning gave near-total immunity, holding against re-evolved payloads; viruses persisted mainly when written into SOUL.md
entries.gaps: Short horizons, one payload-evolution method and LLM-judge infection; no parent-child merge step.

entries.title: Position: Stop Acting Like Language Model Agents Are Normal Agents
entries.gaps: Proposes measuring identity properties but measures nothing.

entries.title: Policy Teaching via Environment Poisoning: Training-time Adversarial Attacks against Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Alters rewards or transition dynamics the agent experiences in training
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box: knows the true MDP
entries.defender_assumptions: No defence; offline planner or online UCRL learner
entries.setup: Undiscounted infinite-horizon MDPs; convex/non-convex programs; 4-state navigation MDP, 10 runs
entries.metric: attack cost; fraction of rounds deviating from target
entries.headline: Dynamics attacks became infeasible beyond margin 0.85 while reward attacks stayed feasible at rising cost
entries.gaps: Single small tabular learner; no multiple sources or k-of-n.

entries.title: Security applications: Lessons of real-world deployment
entries.attacker_access: Observes the defender's randomised schedule through surveillance
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows committed distribution
entries.defender_assumptions: Committed randomised policy (Bayesian Stackelberg); user overrides possible
entries.setup: Deployed systems ARMOR (LAX, since Aug 2007), IRIS (FAMS pilot 2009), GUARDS (TSA, testing)
entries.headline: Only qualitative outcome evidence (police reported more arrests after ARMOR), no counts or control
entries.gaps: Deployment note with no security measurement.

entries.title: Social contagion of memory
entries.attacker_access: Scripted confederate reports non-present items during collaborative recall
entries.setup: Subject-confederate pairs; six household scenes; 15 s vs 60 s viewing; schema-consistent vs less consistent intrusions; individual recall after delay
entries.headline: Effect larger with 15 s encoding and schema-consistent intrusions (numbers not in abstract)
entries.gaps: Scripted dyads with no network spread or artificial agents.

entries.title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge
entries.defender_assumptions: Git provenance, diff, replay, revert of memory commits
entries.setup: Five memory stores (none, markdown, vector DB, graph, git); GPQA-Diamond and MATH-500; two open-weight backbone sizes; pre-registered replications
entries.headline: Cross-problem memory did not reliably help with any store; gains only for near-duplicates (cosine >~0.8); git ~15 ms per write
entries.gaps: No adversarial or poisoned memory tested.

entries.title: Stackelberg Security Games: Looking Beyond a Decade of Success
entries.attacker_access: Observes defender's randomised strategy; chooses targets; colluding attacker coalitions in variants
entries.attacker_knowledge: Best-response or bounded-rationality (quantal response) models
entries.defender_assumptions: Committed randomised strategy; mostly known parameters
entries.setup: Survey of deployed SSGs (ARMOR, IRIS, PROTECT, TSA screening, green security)
entries.headline: Defender strategy spaces exceed 10^33 (threat screening), attacker spaces 10^18 (road networks)
entries.gaps: Pre-LLM survey; coalitional games mentioned but not read in detail.

entries.title: Security and Game Theory: Algorithms, Deployed Systems, Lessons Learned
entries.attacker_access: Human adversaries with surveillance of schedules
entries.attacker_knowledge: Observes randomised schedule
entries.defender_assumptions: Randomised schedules weighted by target importance
entries.gaps: Only the publisher page read; attackers are outsiders, not corrupted copies.

entries.title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code
entries.attacker_access: Only content the system may read (web page, local file, image, audio) formatted as a fake error with remediation instructions
entries.attacker_knowledge: Black-box
entries.attacker_goal: integrity: arbitrary code execution (reverse shell), exfiltration
entries.defender_assumptions: Frameworks at defaults; no sandboxing or tool-call validation; no defence evaluated
entries.setup: AutoGen (Magentic-One, Selector, Round-Robin), CrewAI, MetaGPT; GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Flash; 10 trials per configuration (40 for add-ons, 200 for paraphrase); baseline AgentDojo-style IPI
entries.headline: Web Redirect reverse shell with GPT-4o: 58-90% across orchestrators vs 0-1% for AgentDojo-style IPI baselines; local malicious file on Magentic-One 97%
entries.gaps: Small trial counts, older models, and no defence or k-of-n agreement among children.

entries.title: FlipIt: The Game of Stealthy Takeover
entries.attacker_access: Stealthy takeover of one resource by paying to move at any time
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive renewal or adaptive last-move (learns defender's last move time)
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender can reset at cost; neither learns control until moving
entries.setup: Continuous-time two-player game; renewal processes; dominance analysis; simulation
entries.metric: fraction of time in control minus move costs
entries.headline: Periodic-with-random-phase strongly dominates fixed-rate renewal strategies; exponential defender forces last-move attacker to periodic play
entries.gaps: One resource with no threshold or merge.

entries.title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Direct prompt injection of misinformation, tool-based injection (InjecAgent), memory poisoning (PoisonRAG) on some agents
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive; mimicking attackers not evaluated
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender sees utterance graph (who said what to whom); labelled attack data for supervised GNN; prunes flagged agents' edges
entries.setup: GPT-4o-mini debate MAS with set edge densities and fixed rounds; chain, tree and high-connectivity topologies; CSQA, MMLU; trained on 8-agent systems, transferred to larger and to LLaMA-3.1-70B, Claude-3.5-haiku, DeepSeek-V3; SentenceBERT/MiniLM embeddings
entries.metric: attack success after three rounds; detection accuracy
entries.headline: Attack success fell on average ~18-20% in chain/tree and ~25% in high-connectivity topologies after three rounds
entries.gaps: Reactive, supervised on the tested attack types, no adaptive attacker, and assumes full attribution.

entries.title: Report to the President of the United States (Unclassified Version), Chapter 1: Iraq
entries.attacker_access: Single fabricating source (Curveball) whose reports reached the US only through a foreign liaison intermediary
entries.attacker_goal: integrity (fabrication; own motives, not a controlling adversary per report)
entries.defender_assumptions: Intermediary treated itself as a conduit with no vetting duty; analysts can check only internal consistency
entries.setup: Official investigation with classified access, interviews, comparison with Iraq Survey Group
entries.headline: Almost 100 reports from one source (Jan 2000-Sep 2001) moved assessments from 'could have' to 'has' with high confidence in the Oct 2002 NIE
entries.gaps: Institutional case study with no controlling adversary and no measured remedy.

entries.title: Cowpox: Towards the Immunity of VLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: White-box access to one patient-zero agent; adversarial image virus in retrieval album spread by pairwise chats
entries.attacker_knowledge: White-box to patient zero; adaptive virus re-optimised against captured cure at round 65
entries.defender_assumptions: ~3% defender-controlled Cowpox agents that can optimise cure images outscoring the virus in retrieval
entries.setup: LLaVA-1.5-7B, CLIP retrieval, history 3, album 10, 64 chat rounds, 128 agents with 4 Cowpox agents (Gu et al. setup)
entries.metric: current and cumulative infection; output-analysis accuracy
entries.headline: 4 Cowpox agents in 128 recovered over 95% of infected agents; cumulative infection ~90% instead of 100%
entries.gaps: One retrieval-driven attack family; assumes cure can always outscore virus.

entries.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Corruptions via Node Contribution Backpropagation
entries.attacker_access: One adversarial agent injects plausible wrong content (default attack from Amayuelas et al. 2024); five corruption types
entries.attacker_knowledge: Default non-adaptive; adaptive variants falsify agreement scores or use full system knowledge (intermittently correct answers)
entries.defender_assumptions: Honest majority anchors the final decision; defender sees the signed communication DAG
entries.setup: GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3; MMLU (5 subjects, 100 questions each), Alpaca, Samsum, ChatDoctor; 5 agents, flat and hierarchical, static and dynamic graphs; 3 runs; baseline G-Safeguard
entries.headline: GPT-4o MMLU flat: 88.4% clean, 76.3% attacked, 85.4% with BPD vs 83.7% G-Safeguard; identification 90.7% vs 88.3%
entries.gaps: Small systems with one attacker by default; anchor fails once corrupted agents are the majority.

entries.title: Playing Along: Learning a Double-Agent Defender for Belief Steering via Theory of Mind
entries.attacker_access: Attacker LLM converses with defender to extract sensitive information
entries.attacker_knowledge: Partial prior knowledge in hard scenarios; four attackers incl. stronger OOD ones
entries.defender_assumptions: Defender LLM trained with RL on fooling and theory-of-mind rewards
entries.setup: ToM-SB benchmark; Gemini3-Pro, GPT-5.4 prompted baselines; six defender methods; details not read
entries.gaps: Dialogue secret-keeping, not a turned sub-agent being merged; abstract only.

entries.title: Timing of pre-retrieval warnings matters in reducing memory errors in a repeated testing misinformation study
entries.attacker_access: Misleading post-event narrative
entries.defender_assumptions: General warning about narrative quality, immediate or delayed 24 h
entries.setup: Two behavioural experiments; event, 24 h delay, optional initial test, misleading narrative, warning, final test at two delays; sizes not read
entries.headline: Immediate warning reduced RES; warning delayed 24 hours did not
entries.gaps: Human general warnings only, abstract depth.

entries.title: When Truth Is Distributed: Misinformation Derails Collective Fact Recovery in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: The key-role agent holding exclusive endpoint evidence deceives (fabricated move, overstated window, re-dated report)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Knows ground truth (worst case)
entries.attacker_goal: integrity of collective fact recovery; persistence after exit
entries.defender_assumptions: Honest majority with one second honest key witness; observers without first-hand evidence
entries.setup: ForesightSafety-TIDE: 120 stories, 5 agents each seeing different time windows, 2 key roles observed endpoint; paired honest/deceptive runs; testimony, private votes, 3 public rounds; deception types Event/Coverage/Source (40 each); GPT-5.5, DeepSeek-v4-pro, Grok-4.5 homogeneous systems; exit ablations
entries.metric: truth recovery rate; evidence adoption and relay depth
entries.headline: Truth recovery fell from 72.50% (honest) to 14.17% with one deceiver
entries.gaps: One deceiver, synthetic stories, homogeneous models; no merge into a separate parent.

entries.title: NetSafe: Exploring the Topological Safety of Multi-agent Networks
entries.attacker_access: One or more attacker nodes whose system prompt instructs spreading misinformation, stereotypes or harmful content
entries.attacker_knowledge: Prompted only, non-adaptive
entries.defender_assumptions: Benign agents' alignment; topology choice
entries.setup: RelCom message passing; six-node chain, cycle, binary tree, star, complete graphs; ten rounds; 1-5 attackers; GPT-4o-mini (GPT-3.5-Turbo for harmful); three runs per setting; Fact (153), CSQA subset (127), GSMath subset (113), bias statements, AdvBench
entries.metric: per-agent and joint accuracy per round; moderation score
entries.headline: Complete graph on GSMath fell from 89.38 accuracy with no attackers to 44.25 with five attackers; bias/harmful content blocked even at 5/6 attackers
entries.gaps: Six nodes, one model family and prompt-defined attackers; no exclusive-evidence parts or merge into a parent.

entries.title: Robust Policy Gradient against Strong Data Corruption
entries.attacker_access: Arbitrarily corrupts rewards and transitions at every step of up to an epsilon fraction of episodes
entries.attacker_knowledge: Adaptive in theory; experiments use simple reward flip and scale by delta
entries.defender_assumptions: Robust regression (SEVER) filter inside natural policy gradient; linear Q, exploratory start for theory
entries.setup: FPG (TRPO-based) on six MuJoCo tasks, 3 seeds, epsilon=0.01 of episodes, delta 1-64 tuned per algorithm (also delta=100 on HalfCheetah)
entries.headline: At 1% corrupted episodes vanilla TRPO failed completely (delta=64), while FPG matched clean TRPO performance
entries.gaps: Corruption fraction is per episode rather than per source, with a non-optimised attack.

entries.title: Cut the Crap: An Economical Communication Pipeline for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Agent prompt attack (corrupts role prompts) and agent replacement attack (corrupts generation)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Simple non-adaptive attacks; well-behaved warm-up attacker not addressed
entries.defender_assumptions: Learned sparse, low-rank pruned communication graph fixed after warm-up
entries.setup: AgentPrune; five GPT-4 agents (also gpt-3.5-turbo); MMLU, GSM8K, MultiArith, SVAMP, AQuA, HumanEval; integrated into AutoGen and GPTSwarm
entries.headline: 3.5-10.8% performance improvement over undefended systems under the two attacks; MMLU comparable at $5.6 vs $43.7
entries.gaps: Robustness is a side effect, tested with two simple attacks and no patient attacker.

entries.title: AgentWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems
entries.attacker_access: A single message, shared URL, or poisoned marketplace skill that persuades a victim agent to write the payload into its own configuration (SOUL.md/AGENTS.md)
entries.attacker_knowledge: Hand-designed payloads; black-box to backends
entries.attacker_goal: persistence across restarts, execution, onward propagation
entries.defender_assumptions: Default OpenClaw configs; tested prompt-level templates, execution allowlists, Docker sandbox that discards AGENTS.md writes
entries.setup: Multiple unmodified OpenClaw 2026.3.12 instances on one host with simulated relay; 3 vectors x 3 benign payloads x 5 backends (Minimax-M2.5, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, Nemotron-3-Super, Kimi-K2.5); 2,250 trials; up to 8 turns and 3 attempts per trial; multi-hop chains 30 per vector up to 5 hops; port to Hermes Agent (20 trials per payload); GitHub config census
entries.metric: success rate per phase (persistence, execution, propagation); chain length
entries.headline: Aggregate 63% success; skill supply-chain vector 82%; Docker sandbox took all phases to 0.00 while prompt defences cut success only from 0.65 to 0.37
entries.gaps: Single-host default testbed with stand-in payloads; no parent that merges multiple children's outputs.

entries.title: Adaptive Reward-Poisoning Attacks against Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Changes each reward by delta_t with |delta_t| <= Delta during online learning
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive (transition only) or adaptive (observes learner's Q-table)
entries.attacker_goal: force target policy on chosen states
entries.defender_assumptions: Tabular epsilon-greedy Q-learning; certified safe if Delta below action-gap threshold
entries.setup: Chain and grid MDPs; attack policies learned with TD3; five-state chain, 1000 trials, 10^5 steps
entries.headline: Five-state chain: non-adaptive attack ~9,430 non-target rounds in 10^5 steps vs 30.4 for adaptive
entries.gaps: Magnitude threshold on a single learner, not a count of corrupted sources.

entries.title: Corruption-Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning
entries.attacker_access: Arbitrarily modifies an epsilon fraction of offline (s,a,r,s') tuples; can concentrate budget on least-sampled pair
entries.attacker_knowledge: Worst case (Huber contamination)
entries.defender_assumptions: Robust regression oracles + pessimism; knowledge of epsilon needed without coverage; coverage xi
entries.setup: Linear MDPs of dimension d, horizon H; theory only in parts read
entries.headline: No algorithm can beat Omega(epsilon d H) gap; robustness impossible when d >= 1/epsilon
entries.gaps: Worst-case linear theory with no experiments in parts read.

entries.title: CORBA: Contagious Recursive Blocking Attacks on Multi-Agent Systems Based on Large Language Models
entries.attacker_access: Prompt injected at one entry agent instructing it to block and recursively forward the instruction
entries.attacker_knowledge: Black-box; benign-looking instructions
entries.defender_assumptions: No defence studied
entries.setup: AutoGen and Camel; GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, Gemini 2.0 Flash; 3, 5, 10 agents; varied topologies; open-ended six-agent dialogue; broadcast baseline
entries.headline: 10 agents GPT-4o-mini: 79% (AutoGen) and 92% (Camel) blocked vs 52% and 64% for broadcast baseline
entries.gaps: Availability only with no defence and no merge step.

entries.title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
entries.attacker_access: Prompt injection, adversarial perturbations (GCG, VIPER, SCPN) or demonstrations via user input, intermediate tool output, or memory
entries.attacker_knowledge: Black-box mostly
entries.attacker_goal: DoS / malfunction (infinite loops, irrelevant benign function)
entries.defender_assumptions: LLM self-examination detector
entries.setup: ToolEmu-style emulator with many toolkits; LangChain Gmail and CSV agents; multi-agent chains; GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, Claude-2; failure judged by agent self-reflection with human spot checks
entries.metric: failure rate; propagation rate; detection rate
entries.headline: Infinite-loop injection raised GPT-3.5-Turbo failure from 15.3% to 59.4%; self-examination caught 0% of loop/incorrect-function injections in most settings; memory-route injection 0%
entries.gaps: Two implemented agents with small multi-agent case counts; memory loaded as data, not instructions.

entries.title: INFA-Guard: Mitigating Malicious Propagation via Infection-Aware Safeguarding in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Prompt injection, InjecAgent tool attacks, PoisonRAG memory attacks on attacker agents that then infect benign ones
entries.attacker_knowledge: Non-adaptive
entries.defender_assumptions: Supervised three-class detector on utterance graph with labelled synthesised dialogues; replaces attackers and corrects infected agents; at least one round before acting
entries.setup: GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-235B-A22B; chain, tree, star; CSQA etc. from G-Safeguard benchmark; scaling to 20 and 50 agents; MiniLM embeddings
entries.headline: GPT-4o-mini InjecAgent round-3 ASR 67.5 (none), 13.1 (G-Safeguard), 2.1 (INFA-Guard)
entries.gaps: Supervised and same benchmark family as baselines, no adaptive attacker, empirical not provable threshold.

entries.title: Achilles Heel of Distributed Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Third-party agent provider behind an API: swaps in weaker model, injects noise, uses jailbreak 'dark traits' prompts, returns malicious code; plus delay and disconnection
entries.attacker_knowledge: Simple prompted attacks
entries.attacker_goal: free riding, integrity, code execution (leak files, kill processes), DoS
entries.defender_assumptions: Central controller cannot see inside agents; frameworks mostly trust sub-agents
entries.setup: AutoGen, Camel, AgentVerse, MAD, Reflexion, ChatDev, CrewAI; HumanEval, MMLU (175), MATH (196), Trivia Creative Writing; GPT-4o default, temperature 0; LLaMA substitutes; single malicious agent; three repeats
entries.metric: task performance drop; attack success; malicious code execution rate
entries.headline: Injected malicious code executed in 100% of trials in Reflexion and AutoGen (~41% CrewAI); swapping GPT-4o for LLaMA-2-7B cut performance >60% in less resilient frameworks
entries.gaps: Simple attacks, one malicious agent, no defences beyond retries.

entries.title: Demonstrations of Integrity Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems
entries.attacker_access: Malicious agent's crafted prompts or replaced outputs, including fake system notifications appended to normal outputs
entries.attacker_knowledge: Hand-written templates; knows other agents' roles
entries.attacker_goal: integrity of credit/reputation/tool choice (self-dealing, free-riding, scapegoating, boasting) while end task works
entries.defender_assumptions: LLM monitor (GPT-4o-mini default, o3-mini small test) scoring contributions, even when told of the attacks
entries.setup: CAMEL, AutoGen, MetaGPT; HumanEval, CIAR, MMLU-College; GPT-family agents
entries.metric: percentage change in personal/collective monitor scores; tool choice; token use; task performance
entries.headline: Scapegoater lowered target's monitor scores by 18-67% (personal) with end-task performance moving at most ~6%; warned monitor still failed to detect
entries.gaps: Academic frameworks with hand-written templates and only a preliminary defence.
